Subject: Follow-up: Logging redaction & request/response logs (FinTechCo)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo and for walking through FinTechCo's logging/privacy concerns earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the technical workshop: 

Summary of call:
- Primary ask: prevent PII (names, SSNs, payment instrument PANs) from being stored in request/response logs while preserving enough context for debugging.
- Regulatory constraints: logs cannot contain full PII; retention window likely 30 days (TBD by Legal).
- Traceability: you want trace IDs to help debug cross-service flows, but trace IDs must not be linkable to raw customer identifiers in logs.

Clarifying questions:
1) Which specific fields do you consider PII for logs? (e.g., full names, email addresses, masked emails okay?)
2) Are there header values you must retain for audit (e.g., correlation-id, x-request-id) or can we store hashed/pseudonymized versions?
3) Retention: is 30 days a hard requirement or a starting point? Any regulatory holds or legal holds we should anticipate?

Proposed immediate options (we can demo these in the workshop):
- Client-side masking: remove or mask PII at the SDK/agent before sending to Redwood.
- Runtime redaction filters: configurable rules to redact patterns (SSN regex, credit card PAN) from request/response bodies and headers.
- Trace ID pseudonymization: store a hashed trace id (SHA256 prefix) and keep mapping only in ephemeral debug mode under opt-in.
- Redaction + sample logs export: provide a sanitized sample for debugging with exact lines removed.

I've attached a short design doc (redwood-logging-redaction.pdf) that outlines the runtime options and configuration toggles.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical workshop with your infra/security + our runtime team (30-60m) to align on PII definitions and acceptable pseudonymization.
- Draft a configuration template we can drop into your staging env to demo redaction.

Can you confirm availability for a workshop next week (we're flexible Tue/Thu mornings PT)? Also please reply with any must-have header fields or retention constraints.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the summary and the doc — very helpful. A few answers up front: 

- PII scope: full names, full email addresses, SSNs, full PANs, and unmasked payment tokens are treated as PII. Masked emails (e.g., j***@example.com) are acceptable. IP addresses are acceptable to store for security) but we prefer to limit geolocation derived attributes.
- Headers: must retain a correlation id for investigating multi-service requests. We are OK with a hashed/pseudonymized correlation id as long as it is stable per request and reproducible for debugging when we provide the original trace id under a legal-approved process.
- Retention: 30 days is our target lower-bound for customer-facing logs. For audit logs (who accessed what), Legal may ask for 365 days — they will clarify.

Legal here is looping in the attached high-level requirements (SLA-dataprotection-draft.docx). If you can map your redaction options to the numbered items in that doc it will speed review.

Workshop: Tue 3 Aug or Thu 5 Aug both work for us in the morning PT. Prefer Tue if possible. Please include your runtime engineer so we can get into example logs.

Thanks,

Alex —

Great, thanks for the clarifications. We'll run with 30 days as the demo retention and note audit logs as a separate legal ask. Confirming Tue 3 Aug 10:00 AM PT for the workshop — invite to follow.

Below are the pragmatic options we'll bring to the workshop with a proposed tradeoff summary: 

1) Client-side masking (best privacy, requires SDK changes)
- Pros: PII never reaches our runtime; simplest for compliance.
- Cons: Requires you to upgrade agents/SDKs; may miss server-generated PII.

2) Runtime redaction filters (configurable rules)
- Pros: Flexible, pattern-based, no SDK changes required.
- Cons: Risk of false negatives; need test harness for prompt-based extraction patterns.

3) Header pseudonymization/hashing (recommended for trace IDs)
- Approach: store stable hash (sha256 truncated) of trace/correlation-id; allow a time-limited lookup service under subpoena/legal request.
- Pros: Maintains useful debugging breadcrumbs while removing direct linkability.
- Cons: Lookup introduces a controlled access path with audit logs.

4) Sampling + redaction for sensitive payloads
- For high-volume endpoints that occasionally contain PII, keep a low-percentage sampled sanitized payload for debugging.

Prep for the workshop:
- Dylan, can you prepare a short runtime demo that shows: (a) request body redaction based on regex rules, (b) header pseudonymization flow, and (c) a sample of sanitized log lines?
- Alex/FinTechCo: please bring 1-2 representative log examples (sanitized) and the Legal doc you attached.

I'll update the shared Drive doc with the tradeoffs and a configuration template prior to the meeting: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-logging-design

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.







—Marissa
